Optimal.Notes: A 5W TDP cap is more than enough to hold a rock-solid 60 fps in all situations, including festivals and late-game farms with many objects. Integer scaling keeps pixel art crisp at the native 1280x800 display.

profiles.Summary: Stardew Valley is a lightweight 2D indie farming RPG that runs exceptionally well on the Steam Deck, easily hitting 60 fps with minimal hardware demands. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, making it a near-perfect handheld experience out of the box.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very low PC minimum requirements (256 MB VRAM, 2 GHz CPU) and the Deck hardware. On your first run, confirm 60 fps holds during a busy festival or a large late-game farm — if it does, the Optimal profile is all you will ever need.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 3W TDP and minimum GPU clock, Stardew Valley runs comfortably at a locked 30 fps — the game is so lightweight that even these extreme limits leave headroom. Integer scaling preserves the pixel-art aesthetic perfectly.

MaxPerformance.Notes: With no TDP or GPU clock limits the game runs completely unconstrained, but the display caps output at 60 Hz anyway; this profile is only marginally useful over Optimal and trades battery life for no practical gain.

Optimal.Notes: A 4 W TDP is more than enough to hold a rock-solid 60 fps in all areas including festivals; Integer scaling keeps the pixel art crisp at native 1280x800. This is the recommended everyday profile for Stardew Valley on Deck.

profiles.Summary: Stardew Valley is a lightweight 2D indie farming RPG that runs exceptionally well on the Steam Deck, easily hitting 60 fps with minimal hardware demand. The game is Steam Deck Verified with full controller support, making it an ideal handheld experience with outstanding battery life.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's minimal PC requirements (2 GB RAM, 256 MB VRAM, shader model 3.0) and the known behaviour of lightweight 2D pixel-art games on Deck hardware. On first run, confirm the game holds your chosen frame cap in a crowded festival scene — it almost certainly will, so feel free to push to 90 Hz if you enjoy the smoother feel.

MaxBattery.Notes: Stardew Valley is so lightweight that even a 3 W TDP and minimum GPU clock deliver a locked 30 fps; Integer scaling preserves the pixel-art look perfectly at native resolution. This profile prioritises marathon sessions over raw smoothness.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The OLED Deck's 90 Hz panel makes Stardew Valley feel noticeably smoother during fast inventory and UI interactions; the game is light enough that 7 W comfortably sustains 90 fps everywhere. Battery life is still respectable for such a lightweight title.
